# EKV 2.6 revision 15 intrinsic reference

The DC fixture is an independently executed Verilog-A/OSDI witness, not
generated by the Rust implementation.

- Reference: [ekv26/model](https://github.com/ekv26/model/tree/137e7779c66d282113ce5802843f546869cb8c05), file ekv26_SDext_Verilog-A.va; see crate NOTICE.
- Compiler: OpenVAF-reloaded 23.5.0, OSDI 0.4, build 89-g04940bf.
- Simulator: ngspice 47, at 27 degrees Celsius; reference TNOM defaults to 25.
- Set all three extended-reference junction saturation currents and junction
  capacitances to zero; RSH defaults to zero. This isolates intrinsic channel
  and impact current, without asserting that the extended diode law is PSpice.
- Tight absolute current tolerance is required for sub-pA sweeps. At
  Vg = -0.25 V, an independent operating point gives 1.2883662830837392e-13 A,
  whereas the default-tolerance sweep reports 3.7124228236470870e-14 A.
- The Verilog-A thermal-voltage probe at 27 degrees Celsius returns
  0.02586492315346030 V (CODATA 2010 k/q).

Regenerate in a scratch directory with the reference source and
reference-dc.cir:

```sh
openvaf-r ekv26_SDext_Verilog-A.va -o ekv.osdi
ngspice -b reference-dc.cir
```

Source currents in the fixture enter the ideal voltage sources, opposite
to the device residual convention.

The linearization fixture is generated by generate-intrinsic.sh in the same
scratch directory. It records exact operating-point residuals and four
independent ideal-voltage-source excitations at 1 MHz. Imaginary current
divided by angular frequency gives each charge Jacobian column. The cases
span both polarities, reversed drain/source, equal drain/source, -40 to
125 degrees Celsius, short and long geometry, segmented channel, both
mobility laws, weak inversion and impact ionization.

The two noise decks use a controlled current source driven by the clamped
drain voltage source and a noiseless 1-ohm output resistor. The output
spectral amplitude therefore equals the drain current noise amplitude.
One deck isolates channel thermal noise; the other enables flicker noise
with coefficient 1e-25 and frequency exponent 1.2.

The transient fixture independently integrates the displacement currents
during a 1.5 V gate ramp over 1 microsecond, with a maximum 5 ns step.
Subtract the DC residual from each source current, integrate the remaining
current with trapezoidal quadrature and compare the terminal charge change
to the intrinsic model. The first OP sample is omitted because it does
not have ramp displacement current.
